propositions: Ubuntu Verified jobs occupy 30.2 runner-minutes per run across three Python cells (py3.11/3.12/3.13) with recurring >30s operations: bridge-cadence YAML parsing 1,440× per test, Pandoc corpus subprocess redundancy across two harness files, AST provenance fixture recomputation, and complexity-policy repeated invocation.

Bridge cadence test reads and parses the same workflow YAML inside a 1,440-minute comprehension loop, consuming 7.653s of the measured 7.925s baseline; hoisting the parse restores the prior invariant-loading pattern and saves estimated 5.70 runner-minutes per Verified run without changing the exhaustive proof.

Pandoc hardening oracle runs both current and legacy _convert via subprocess for all 884 units but asserts only legacy output identity; replacing the 883 redundant legacy subprocesses with immutable expected outputs preserves all real Pandoc product conversions and coverage while saving estimated runner-contention cost.

Static Pandoc corpus plus small real contract sample with full replay in External Integration workflow meets OSS consensus (Pandoc, nbconvert, pypandoc, Kubernetes, Rust precedent) while superseding ADR 0095's test-assurance sentence and preserving production segmentation, safety invariants, and assertion classes.

Editor loopback fixture setup recurs at 35.0–35.1s as the only Ubuntu individual test phase consistently exceeding 30s; instrumentation attributes it to socket.getfqdn and nested socket.bind calls on macOS, distinguishable from test logic by nested runtime decomposition.

Verified job admission cancellation regressed under always() predicates in full-route reusable jobs; replacing with cancellation-aware !cancelled() status checks removes 1,500+ second waits for superseded runs while preserving classifier-failure fallback and all successful-patchset jobs.
